clue.text: Disengage from the faithful? Awful clues result

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the letters of the word clues are jumbled

parts.note: to arise is to result or follow on as a consequence

explanation.surface: A setter is told that dreadful clues will drive away the devoted solvers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' is the anagram signal. 'The faithful' looks like loyal solvers of the puzzle, but it means religious believers, and taking something out of their hands makes it worldly.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something non-religious is to detach it from believers, a playful way of describing removing church control.

clue.text: Piece of furniture not finished until now

indicators.note: not finished says the phrase loses its final letter, so the end is cut off

parts.note: so far is an idiom meaning up to the present

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a piece of furniture has still not been completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not finished' trims the R from SO FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch for seating several people is a common item of household furniture.

clue.text: A vehicle almost surrounded by others in SA city

indicators.note: surrounded by says the preceding pieces sit inside the word for others

parts.note: following on from vehicle, the others are more cars

indicators.note: almost says the vehicle word loses its final letter

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car is boxed in by traffic in a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims the vehicle and 'surrounded by' puts the pieces inside 'others', read as more vehicles following on from the first. SA is South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracas is the capital of Venezuela, a nation of South America.

clue.text: Lots, initially, on this person's plate

definitions.text: Lots, initially, on this person's plate

parts.words: Lots, initially, on this person's plate
parts.note: in Britain a novice motorist must display an L plate, and L is the first letter of lots

explanation.surface: Someone has a heavy workload, plenty on their plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On one's plate' means a workload, but here it is the British L plate a novice motorist must display; L is the initial of 'Lots'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person learning to drive in the UK carries a plate bearing the letter L, the initial letter of lots.

clue.text: International organization of revolutionary movements

definitions.meaning: ... International is a worldwide service club for business people
turning round an axis, as a wheel's motion does, is described by this adjective

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics, but here it means turning round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: The service club takes its name from members meeting in rotation, and the adjective describes spinning motion.

clue.text: Mocking what eager consumer is doing

definitions.meaning: ... at someone means jeering at them
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, a British informal sense

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from scoff: to jeer, and, in British slang, to wolf down food.

clue.text: Conservative, left of centre — what's the catch?

indicators.note: left of means the first piece is placed before the second in an across entry

parts.note: a hub is a centre of activity

explanation.surface: A Tory politician of left-leaning views is asked what the snag is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left of centre' reads as politics, but it places C to the left of HUB. 'Catch' is something caught by an angler.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish, so it is something an angler might land.

clue.text: In very short time, 25% of amount?

definitions.text: In very short time, 25% of amount?

parts.words: In very short time, 25% of amount?
parts.note: a phrase meaning in a moment, read literally, takes half of the first half of the word amount, so a quarter of it

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a quick quarter share of a sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of 'amount' is AMO, so half of that half, 'half a mo', is a quarter of the word; the phrase itself is British for 'in a moment'.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal phrase for a brief moment, as in wait a second.

clue.text: Cruel queen that may be drunk

definitions.meaning: Mary I of England earned the nickname for burning Protestants
a cocktail of vodka and tomato juice carries the queen's nickname

explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of Mary Tudor is also the name of a vodka and tomato juice cocktail.

clue.text: London paper covering regions in distant part of world

indicators.note: covering says the paper's letters go round the outside of the regions

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, published in London
areas are regions

explanation.surface: A London newspaper reports on far-off parts of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern Asia is a remote region of the world from a European viewpoint, the usual name for it.

clue.text: Part of plot he'll outline for play

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dramatist sketches a portion of the storyline for a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for play' as the definition; 'for' is only a link, so the definition is 'play'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy about the Moor of Venice is a famous stage drama.

clue.text: In southern parts, arranged box or other tree

indicators.note: in says the box word is placed inside the rearranged letters
parts suggests the word is split up and its letters broken apart
arranged says the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: a chest is a box

explanation.surface: In the South, box hedges and other trees have been planted in rows.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUTHERN is rearranged into HORSE NUT ('parts', 'arranged') and CHEST goes 'In' it. 'Box' is also a tree, which is why 'or other tree' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: This large tree bears the shiny brown seeds British children call conkers.

clue.text: Recent misbehaving by brazen footballer

indicators.note: misbehaving suggests letters getting out of line, so the word is jumbled

parts.note: forward means bold or presumptuous

explanation.surface: A footballer has lately been behaving badly and shamelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The central attacking player in a football team plays in this position.

clue.text: Rich man not drinking with people inside — getting out of habit?

parts.note: Dives is the traditional name of the rich man in the Bible parable of Lazarus

indicators.note: inside says the people word sits within the abstinence letters

parts.note: TT is teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
men are people

explanation.surface: A wealthy man who gives up alcohol with friends around is breaking a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like a routine, but it is clothing; disposing of something, like shedding a monk's habit, is the definition's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Divesting means stripping off or disposing of something, so taking off a robe is a playful example.

clue.text: Not reacting about second piece put in

indicators.note: about says the inactive word goes round the letter for second

parts.note: inert means chemically unreactive

explanation.surface: A passive person is asked about a second section that was added.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra section placed within something, such as a leaflet in a magazine, is this noun.

clue.text: New café moving a place for waiters

indicators.note: moving says the letter a shifts to a new position in the assembled word

parts.note: a tearoom is a café

explanation.surface: A new café is relocating, which is a place for its waiting staff.
explanation.walkthrough: N plus TEAROOM gives NTEAROOM; 'moving' sends the A to the front. 'Waiters' is not restaurant staff but people waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room before a main one where visitors wait to be received, a waiting room.

clue.text: GOP's side corruptly spread malicious rumours

indicators.note: corruptly suggests something debased, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A corrupt faction of the Republican Party put about slander.
explanation.walkthrough: GOP is the US Republican Party; 'corruptly' rearranges GOPS and SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on idle talk about other people, often unkind, is the meaning.

clue.text: One making slow progress in French course — bad mark in English obtained

definitions.text: One making slow progress in French course

indicators.note: in says the blemish word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: got means obtained
a scar is a bad mark on the skin

explanation.surface: A slow learner of French gets a poor mark in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French course' looks like a language class, but it is a course of a meal; the snail is the slow mover.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail, which moves slowly, served as a dish in French cooking.

clue.text: Abandon in cold, with nothing on

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
with all clothes off means naked

explanation.surface: Someone gives up going out in the cold wearing no clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel an event or plan is to abandon it.

clue.text: Demonstrator's derogatory term for group

definitions.meaning: one who shows or displays something
in British slang a hopeless or contemptible bunch of people is called this

explanation.walkthrough: The British informal sense calls a useless bunch 'a right shower'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who shows is literally a shower, while British slang uses the word to scorn a hopeless lot.

clue.text: Damages highest point on mount

definitions.meaning: to wither is to shrivel or blight something
the ridge between a horse's shoulder blades is the top of its back

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a mountain, but it is a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Blights shrivel plants, and the ridge between a horse's shoulders shares the same spelling.

clue.text: Skill with point got me!

parts.note: a deft touch is a skill
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A fencer's skill with the sword's tip draws a hit and an admission.
explanation.walkthrough: In fencing, the word is said to acknowledge a hit; more widely, a good point scored.
explanation.definitionFit: The French fencing call admits a hit, used in English to concede a clever riposte.

clue.text: Soap dispenser?

parts.note: soap here means a soap opera, delivered to viewers by a household screen

explanation.walkthrough: A soap dispenser sits by the sink, but soap here is a soap opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The household box that broadcasts drama serials dispenses soap operas.

clue.text: I had heard and observed

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken, and their sound gives a differently spelt word

parts.note: the contraction for I had is I'd

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have heard and seen something.
explanation.definitionFit: Having looked at something is to have watched it, a synonym for noted by sight.

clue.text: European taking journey after journey as boost for confidence

indicators.note: after says the second journey word is placed following the first

parts.note: to go is to make a journey
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A European travels repeatedly to feel better about themself.
explanation.definitionFit: An activity done chiefly to flatter oneself is an idiom for something that boosts one's self-esteem.

clue.text: Knowing about monarch preserving business

indicators.note: about says the shrewd word goes round the monarch's letters

parts.note: canny means shrewd or knowing
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A shrewd adviser to the sovereign protects a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserving' looks like protecting, but it means canning food.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory that seals food in tins is a business that preserves.

clue.text: Desired a TV broadcast to be made known

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wanted a television programme to be publicised.
explanation.definitionFit: To promote or announce something publicly is to make it widely known.
